- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2) in recent days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after sentiment spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 2σ above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15% for next period; if below, increase by 5–10%.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply downward adjustment of 2–5% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low swings, model tends to misalign with true trend; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
